narrative_purpose: Show the tugs doing the one thing buoyancy cannot: supplying heading. They fly crosswind arcs on long lines while the vast bell yaws slowly behind them.
subject: Six flattened ray-shaped flying animals with broad rippling pectoral margins, each with a tiny blue-skinned rider, flying ahead of and across the path of a large translucent Medusoid bell. Each is connected to the bell's forward harness by a long taut fibre towline. The rays are banked over in sweeping curved paths that cut sideways across the frame rather than pointing straight ahead, their lines fanning out. Behind them the great bell is angled slightly, beginning a slow turn.
scene: High open sky over a distant cloud layer, the whole group in level flight with long empty sky ahead of them.
camera: Three-quarter view from slightly ahead and above, so both the curving flight paths of the tugs and the slow yaw of the bell are legible.
light: Clear high-altitude light, cool and even; faint teal bioluminescent edging along the rays' margins.
palette: Deep indigo and teal sky, pale translucent bell, faint teal glow along the tug animals' rippling edges.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate, dynamic but not action-poster.
detail_level: Crisp on the rays, riders and taut towlines; the bell slightly softer, cloud layer dissolving into haze.
composition: Tug animals across the left and centre in curving arcs, towlines converging back to the bell on the right, generous plain dark sky above framed by deep negative space.
consistency_notes: The tugs must clearly be flying ACROSS the direction of travel in arcs, not pulling in a straight line - that is the physics being taught. They supply no lift, only forward and lateral pull. Bell matches fig-00-cover.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no propellers, no fire, no combat, no 3D-render or photographic look, no cartoon style
